stories.description: A stockroom clerk derives current inventory from an ordered movement journal. Read one JSON request from stdin. A balance request is an object with op equal to balance and movements as an array. Each movement has sku, a nonempty string of uppercase ASCII letters and digits, and delta, a nonzero JSON integer in the inclusive range -1000000 to 1000000 (booleans are invalid). Starting at zero per SKU, apply movements in order. Return {"balances":[{"sku":"SKU","onHand":0}]} with one row for every SKU encountered, including zero balances, sorted by ascending ASCII SKU. An empty journal returns {"balances":[]}. Use src/main.py for Python standard-library stdin/stdout routing and src/ledger.py for movement validation and replay. Emit one JSON value to stdout and exit successfully even for invalid requests.

Reject an invalid request object, unknown operation, missing or malformed movements, or invalid row with exactly {"error":"INVALID_REQUEST"}. Validate the shape of every row before applying any movement. If any intermediate balance becomes negative, return exactly {"error":"NEGATIVE_STOCK","sku":"SKU"} for the first SKU that fails in journal order. A later restock cannot legalize a preceding overdraft.
